newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND A ON TOP AS ENGLAND TOIL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND A ON TOP AS ENGLAND TOIL.

text.p: Pace men Heath Davis and Geoff Allott staked a claim to test places on Friday as New Zealand A bowled out England for 107 and piled on a big second innings lead.
Llorne Howell hit an unbeaten half century as New Zealand A moved to 187-4 in their second innings, an overall lead of 261.

England, resuming at 30 for three and chasing a first innings target of 181, lost four wickets in the space of 36 balls in the first hour as Allott and Davis exploited a pitch with sharp lift and variable bounce.

Craig White fended a short ball from Allott to Phil Chandler at short leg in the fifth over. Hussain fell victim to an unplayable delivery from Davis which exploded off the pitch, clipped the shoulder of his bat and lobbed to Chris Harris at gully.
Only all-rounder Ronnie Irani defied the New Zealand A bowlers with a knock of 40, including seven fours, before being last man out.
Davis finished with four for 22 and Allott claimed four for 44, both men sending a timely message to the New Zealand selectors who are due to name their second test side on Saturday.
England, pounded by press commentators for failing to clinch the first test which ended in a draw earlier this week, saw their misery compounded when New Zealand A batted again.
Darrin Murray was bowled by Andrew Caddick for 12, but fellow-opener Craig Spearman struck a belligerent 47 before being caught by Nick Knight off Irani.
At the close of play on day two of the four-day match, Howell was unbeaten on 51 and with Chris Harris had added an unbroken partnership of 86 for the fifth wicket.
